claims.text: Kyiv came under a new missile attack on Wednesday night, injuring six people according to Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko.
US President Donald Trump stated that settling the war between Russia and Ukraine is getting closer.
US special envoy Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday.
Steve Witkoff met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo on Tuesday prior to visiting St Petersburg.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that he would accept a deal freezing the war along the current front line.
Russian President Vladimir Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov suggested that a new round of talks could be held around November 10 in Abu Dhabi.
Prior to talks with Steve Witkoff, Russia released 74-year-old American Stephen Hubbard, who had been sentenced to nearly seven years in prison for allegedly fighting for Ukraine.
Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the release of American Stephen Hubbard from a Russian prison.
Stephen Hubbard is a 74-year-old former teacher who spent more than four years in Russian jails on charges of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that Stephen Hubbard was released without requiring any prisoner swap in return.
US envoy Steve Witkoff called Russian President Vladimir Putin a humanitarian during their meeting at the Constantine Palace in St Petersburg.
Russian President Vladimir Putin is wanted by the International Criminal Court as a war criminal in relation to the deportation of Ukrainian children.
More than 17,500 civilians have been confirmed killed in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to the UN.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the decision to restrict Ukraine's access to Starshield came from Elon Musk.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine supported a US proposal for three-way negotiator-level talks with Russia and the US no later than early November.
Russian Presidential aide Yury Ushakov stated that Vladimir Putin agreed to resume Washington-mediated peace talks after November 10.
Moscow proposed holding a trilateral summit involving Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November.
New Mexico District Judge Francis Mathew ordered Meta to pay $25 billion following a trial over its Facebook user data practices.
Judge Francis Mathew stated Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations spanned more than 11 years from 2010 to 2021.
Meta's chief legal officer CJ Mahoney stated that Meta intends to appeal the New Mexico court ruling.
A jury found that Meta violated New Mexico state laws more than 40 million times.
New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez stated that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable.
Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle data privacy and child safety claims brought by 48 other US states.
The Cambridge Analytica app 'thisisyourdigitallife' reached roughly 87 million Facebook users worldwide.
New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez called the $25 billion ruling against Meta a historic win.
New Mexico state District Judge Francis Mathew stated that Facebook falsely promised users that they controlled their data.
New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez announced that all penalty money awarded from the Meta judgment will go into a fund for New Mexico's education system.
Judge Francis Mathew ruled that a penalty exceeding $219 billion was warranted against Meta under state law before being reduced to $25 billion.
Jurors determined that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta leadership on privacy and content moderation were misleading.
Jurors found Meta committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection laws.
Judge Francis Mathew ordered that Meta's $25 billion penalty will accrue interest at an annual rate of 15% until paid in full.
French President Emmanuel Macron accused Donald Trump and other foreign leaders of making unacceptable and stupid comments about France's civil unrest.
French President Emmanuel Macron stated that AI-generated images circulating online depicted fake scenes of unrest in France.
Yields on French benchmark 10-year government bonds passed 5% on Wednesday, reaching their highest level since 2002.
Partial night-time curfews were imposed in areas of French cities including Paris, Marseille, and Lille following violent protests and looting.
Research by the NGO Alliance4Europe found that pro-Russian networks manipulated online information to amplify anger in France prior to recent protests.
French President Emmanuel Macron stated in Doha that there was foreign manipulation of information following the French riots.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in an interview that France had been hit by an invasion of extremist Islam.
US President Donald Trump blamed the riots in France on mass immigration.
More than 800 people were brought before courts and nearly 150 jailed in France following the recent riots.
Authorities in Paris and Lyon renewed night-time curfews in central city districts, while Marseille enacted a curfew for unaccompanied minors.
Police in France arrested a suspect in connection with an arson attack that damaged the 143-year-old city hall in Limoges.
French authorities arrested at least 2,400 people following nationwide rioting and clashes with police that began on Saturday.
Australian federal police and ASIO conducted safety briefings with politicians following a car attack on MP Helen Haines.
Reports of harassing and threatening behavior against Australian public office holders received by the AFP increased from 951 two years ago to 1,067 last year.
Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines lost both her legs after a car rammed into her outside her office in Wangaratta.
Driver Brendan Nugent was charged with intentionally harming a commonwealth public official in connection with the attack on Helen Haines.
Local barber Ricky Jefferies intervened in the attack on Helen Haines by tackling and restraining the suspect until police arrived.
Helen Haines was first elected to the Australian parliament in 2019 as an independent MP representing Wangaratta.
Surgeons amputated both legs of 65-year-old Australian MP Helen Haines following a car attack in Wangaratta.
The suspect in the attack on Helen Haines, 43-year-old Brendan N. of Tarrawingee, appeared in Wangaratta Magistrates' Court facing multiple charges including causing harm to a federal official.
Chirag Patel, defense lawyer for suspect Brendan N., told the court that his client suffers from a rare neurological condition, an undiagnosed mental health condition, and a concussion.
Local barber Ricky Jeffries disarmed the suspect of a knife during the attack on MP Helen Haines before holding him down for police.
A drone strike hit the Amiet Market in the disputed Abyei region at around midday on Monday, killing at least 153 people.
South Sudanese officials blamed Sudan's military for the drone strike on Amiet Market in Abyei.
Caretaker Information Minister Yohana Akol Ngor stated that around 8,000 people were displaced by the bombing in Abyei.
The drone strike in Abyei hit a fuel depot at Amiet Market, sparking a massive fire that burned overnight into Tuesday.
Doctors Without Borders (MSF) reported treating over 20 wounded patients, including critical burn cases, at Ameth Bek hospital following the Abyei strike.
A Sudanese military source told the BBC that Sudan's army conducted the drone strike on Amiet Market, claiming it was a fuel supply site for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
Separate drone strikes in West Kordofan state on Sunday evening killed 150 people, including mourners traveling in a truck to a funeral, according to the Sudan War Observatory.
South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest over the drone attack in the disputed Abyei region.
Abyei is a resource-rich border region jointly administered by Sudan and South Sudan, with ownership disputed since South Sudan's independence in 2011.
UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric stated that 20 million people in Sudan face acute hunger amid the ongoing conflict.
Analyst Jan Pospisil from the Peace and Conflict Resolution Evidence Platform stated that neither the Sudanese military nor the RSF demonstrates regard for human life in the conflict.
An Israeli settler was filmed shouting at and assaulting a Palestinian child during an attack on a family east of Yatta in the West Bank.
Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was beaten and seriously injured by a crowd of masked Israeli settlers while covering an olive harvest in Abu Falah.
Heidi Levine sustained four fractured vertebrae, two broken ribs, and four puncture wounds during the settler attack.
Witnesses stated that Palestinian youths used slingshots against settlers to allow other reporters to help Heidi Levine to safety.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog called Heidi Levine to express regret and referred to the attackers as thugs.

Israeli security forces declared a closed military zone and detained US Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander alongside dozens of volunteers assisting Palestinian olive harvesters in Nahalin.
Brad Lander was released from Israeli military custody with a warning following his detention.
The Israeli military stated that harvesting in the Nahalin area required prior security requests that were not submitted by local farmers.
Non-profit group New Israel Fund stated that approximately 90 volunteers participating in the Protect the Harvest initiative were released by Wednesday night.
The Israeli military detained approximately 80 US, Israeli, and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Nahalin in the West Bank.
Former Israeli Deputy Attorney General Joshua Schoffman was among those detained by Israeli forces during the olive harvest in Nahalin.
Among the detained volunteers in Nahalin were T'ruah CEO Jill Jacobs and 11 other American rabbis.
